items.title: Petry retires from NHL after 16 seasons
items.summary:
Jeff Petry announced his retirement from the NHL after 16 seasons on Thursday.
The 38-year-old defenseman had nine assists in 67 games with the Florida Panthers and Minnesota Wild last season. He did not have a point in three Stanley Cup Playoff games.
items.body: Defenseman played 1,048 games, including for Panthers, Wild last season Jeff Petry announced his retirement from the NHL after 16 seasons on Thursday. The 38-year-old defenseman had nine assists in 67 games with the Florida Panthers and Minnesota Wild last season. He did not have a point in three Stanley Cup Playoff games. Petry made the announcement on his wife's podcast "Never Offside with Julie & Cat." Selected by the Edmonton Oilers in the second round (No. 45) of the 2006 NHL Draft, Petry had 394 points (96 goals, 298 assists) in 1,048 regular-season games for the Edmonton Oilers, Montreal Canadiens, Pittsburgh Penguins, Detroit Red Wings, Panthers and Wild. He had 13 points (five goals, eight assists) in 51 playoff games and made the Cup Final with the Canadiens in 2020-21 when they lost to the Tampa Bay Lightning in five games. Petry played in his 1,000th game while with the Panthers last season against the Vancouver Canucks on Nov. 17, 2025. "Playing 1,000 games going into last year, that was a goal of mine and to be able to accomplish that was great," he said. The Ann Arbor native, who got to play for his hometown Red Wings for two seasons from 2023-25, also discussed some of his favorite NHL memories. "My first (NHL) game in Edmonton (Dec. 28, 2010)," Petry said. "That dream finally came true. Scoring my first goal (Jan. 20, 2011). The biggest memory was playing in the finals with Montreal. Obviously not the ending result (we wanted), but to be able to do that was special." Petry also represented the United States at the IIHF World Championships four times (2012-2014, 2024), including winning the bronze medal in 2013. items.summary: Given how bad things have gone for the Caps, you can’t just pin their struggles on one thing. There are a handful of problems that are contributing to Washington’s downfall right now.
items.body: If there were a trophy for winning the off-season, it would’ve been awarded to the Washington Capitals this past summer. In a wide-open division outside of the Carolina Hurricanes, the Caps were a trendy pick by some to contend for a division title and maybe even come out of the East. Prior to Wednesday’s desperately needed win over Philadelphia, Washington had lost seven of nine games and five in a row overall, leaving them in 12th place in the Eastern Conference. During that losing streak, the Caps allowed an average of six goals per game. With teams like the New York Rangers and New York Islanders exceeding expectations, along with a good chance of five Atlantic teams making the post-season, Washington is in real danger of falling out of the playoff race if it doesn’t pick it up soon. items.title: Kessel’s love of playing in NHL led to U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame
items.summary: The 2026 U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame induction is Nov. 30. This year's class includes Amanda Kessel, Phil Kessel, T.J. Oshie, Ryan Suter and Stan Wong. Here, NHL.com senior draft writer Mike Morreale profiles Phil Kessel.
items.body: 3-time Cup champ holds ironman streak with 1,064 straight regular-season games The 2026 U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame induction is Nov. 30. This year's class includes Amanda Kessel, Phil Kessel , T.J. Oshie , Ryan Suter and Stan Wong. Here, NHL.com senior draft writer Mike Morreale profiles Phil Kessel. Phil Kessel played through the pain, the bumps, the bruises and all those mornings when he arrived at the rink just not feeling right. He’d play 1,064 consecutive regular-season games, in fact, an NHL Ironman record built over nearly 13 years and five teams. He played through injuries others never knew about, the pressure of being a star and three long Stanley Cup Playoffs runs. Kessel never set out to chase the record. In an interview with NHL Network Radio and during his election press conference, he said he simply hated sitting out. "I don't think it was ever a priority," Kessel said. "I just always wanted to play in the games. I love playing the games. I love playing hockey and I never wanted to miss. "As a player and competitor, you never want to sit out. You never want to be in the stands. You never want to be injured. You always want to be out there." That passion, durability and understated competitiveness helped make Kessel one of the most accomplished American players of his generation. Now, the reluctant superstar and three-time Stanley Cup champion is headed to the U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame. Kessel and his sister, Amanda, an Olympic gold medalist and four-time IIHF Women's World Championship gold medalist, headline the Class of 2026 to be inducted at the dinner and ceremony at the Grand Hyatt Washington in Washington, D.C., on Nov. 30. The Madison, Wisconsin, natives will become the second sister-brother combination inducted, joining Cammi Granato and Tony Granato.

items.body: Register Login Jeff Petry Announces Retirement By Brian La Rose | at November 26, 2026 9:00 pm After being unable to secure a contract for this season, a veteran defenseman is calling it a career. In an appearance on the Never Offside podcast ( video link ), Jeff Petry indicated that he has now retired at the age of 38. Petry was a second-round pick by Edmonton back in 2006, going 45th overall. Four years later, he made the jump to the NHL and by the 2011-12 season, he was a full-fledged regular with the Oilers. He showed plenty of early promise, being thrust into a top-four role right away but never was able to get his offense going with any sort of consistency. That changed following a 2014 trade deadline trade to Montreal. Petry went from only reaching 25 points once over his time with Oilers to hitting the 40-point mark four different seasons with the Canadiens. He spent part of eight years with them before being moved to Pittsburgh in a deal that brought Mike Matheson to Montreal back in 2022. Petry was one-and-done with the Penguins. He had a solid 31-point effort in 61 games in 2022-23 but Pittsburgh needed to clear his contract off the books in order to pursue Erik Karlsson . It took a three-team trade to complete it, with Petry briefly winding up back in Montreal before being flipped to Detroit, allowing him to join his hometown team. Petry got to spend two seasons at home with the Red Wings but by then, his role was starting to change. After being a top-pairing player at times in Montreal, his ice time was starting to be scaled back, and with that, his production. items.title: Schenn, Canucks aiming to revive effort level amid challenging stretch
items.summary: For all the Canucks’ projected problems in Year 1 of the rebuild, effort was not supposed to be one of them.
items.body: PHILADELPHIA – A classic nor-easter storm barrelled into Philadelphia Thursday afternoon for U.S. Thanksgiving, lashing semi-deserted streets with sheets of rain driven sideways by winds gusting up to 80 kilometres per hour. Practising inside a giant hockey arena staffed, it seemed, by a security guard and the Zamboni driver, the Canucks were sheltered from a storm that felt somehow familiar because the National Hockey League’s worst team has been buffeted by severe wind and rain all season. The rebuilding Canucks play Game 28, completing the first third of their season, Friday against the Philadelphia Flyers. Vancouver has six wins. And its 20 regulation losses are five more than the next worst team in the standings, the Pittsburgh Penguins. The volatile weather, of course, was forecast as soon as the Canucks were tipped into the franchise’s first full-scale rebuild this century by the Quinn Hughes trade 11½ months ago. But for all the projected problems, effort was not supposed to be one of them. Nearly two months prior, Stevenson’s career took an unexpected detour through Manitoba after he failed to make the Washington Capitals ’ opening-night roster out of training camp. But after two separate waiver wire transactions, Stevenson found himself back in his old crease at Giant Center, Wednesday night. “Sometimes it’s unpredictable and you have to be adaptable, right?” Stevenson said of his whirlwind start to the season, per FOX43’s Todd Sadowski. “This place obviously holds a really special place in my heart, and it’s really fun to be back here.” In his first game for the Bears since May 7, a 4-1 season-ending loss to the Penguins, Stevenson stopped 28 of 29 shots — some in spectacular fashion — to earn 2nd Star of the Night honors and catapult Hershey back to second place in the Atlantic Division. Stevenson admitted that his return was emotional and felt different than some of previous big starts at Giant Center. “Yeah, it was. It was,” Stevenson said. “I don’t know, maybe almost a little nostalgic. It’s not like I’m that far removed from it. items.title: Brenden Dillon Receives Four-Game Suspension
items.summary: New Jersey Devils defenseman Brenden Dillon has received a four-game suspension for an illegal check to the head on Denton Mateychuk.
items.body: Register Login Brenden Dillon Receives Four-Game Suspension By Brian La Rose | at November 26, 2026 6:00 pm With the Devils having an early afternoon game on Friday, the Department of Player Safety was going to have to make a quick ruling on the fate of Brenden Dillon after his hearing today. They did just that, announcing that the defenseman has received a four-game suspension for his hit on Columbus blueliner Denton Mateychuk . In the video accompanying the announcement, it was noted that Dillon was deemed to have elevated “upward and unnecessarily and making Mateychuk’s head the main point of contact on a hit where such head contact was avoidable” . Because it was deemed avoidable, it became grounds for suspension under Rule 48. Meanwhile, he received a match penalty for the hit, which occurred a little past the midway mark of the first period. It is the second suspension of the 36-year-old’s career, the other coming back in February 2024, also for an illegal check to the head. However, since more than two years had elapsed, he didn’t qualify as a repeat offender for the purpose of salary forfeiture, though the prior act could still be considered when determining the number of games of the suspension. Dillon will forfeit a little over $82K in salary, with that money going to the Players’ Emergency Assistance Fund. Meanwhile, he’ll be eligible to return on December 5th against Pittsburgh. Vladislav Kolyachonok , who scored in his Devils debut two weeks ago, has been serving as the seventh defenseman since then and should draw back into the lineup while Dillon is serving his suspension. items.summary: New Jersey Devils defenceman Brenden Dillon won’t take the ice for the next handful of games.
items.body: New Jersey Devils defenceman Brenden Dillon received a four-game suspension on Thursday for an illegal hit to the head of Columbus Blue Jackets defenceman Denton Mateychuk. Dillon was assessed a match penalty for the check during the first period of the Devils' shootout win in Columbus on Wednesday night. Mateychuk left the game after the hit. Dillon forfeits $82,474.24 based on his average annual salary and under the terms of the collective bargaining agreement. The money goes to the Players’ Emergency Assistance Fund. On the play, Mateychuk skated through neutral ice and entered the zone before moving the puck to a teammate. Once the puck was gone, Dillon finished a “high, hard check, elevating upward and unnecessarily and making Mateychuk's head the main point of contact on a hit where such head contact was avoidable,” the NHL's department of player safety said in a video. Blue Jackets coach Rick Bowness said after the game: "I’ve coached Dillon. He’s not a dirty player. He’s a hard player. He caught him in a bad spot, and that’s a bad hit. items.summary: The Wild can ill afford to waste what might be their final year with Quinn Hughes.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Nick Wosika-Imagn Images The Minnesota Wild are in a tough spot. Just under a year after mortgaging a sizeable chunk of their future to land star defenseman Quinn Hughes from the Vancouver Canucks , the Wild seem no closer to signing the 27-year-old to a new contract. If anything, Wild general manager Bill Guerin sounds less and less confident each time he’s asked about the situation. And yet … from a hockey standpoint, the Wild haven’t given Hughes any reason not to sign with them. As of Thursday, they’re tied with the Carolina Hurricanes atop the NHL standings with 41 points. They’ve won 18 of 27 games this season, along with just four regulation losses. Right now, they have to be the odds-on favorites to come out of the Western Conference. Hughes has missed Minnesota’s last three games with an undisclosed injury, but it shouldn’t be long before he returns to the lineup — and when he’s played, the Wild have given him more freedom than ever. The 5’10” righty has already amassed 34 points (eight goals, 26 assists) in 24 games this season, good for second on the Wild in scoring. He’s also averaging a career-high 27:49 of ice time per game. When healthy, Hughes is right there with Cale Makar in the Norris Trophy race every single year, and Hughes will likely continue to be the standard against which all undersized puck-moving defense prospects are measured until the day he retires. He’s as elusive and dangerous as any player in the league. The Wild have a ton of money coming off the books after this season, and you can bet they’d love nothing more than to give most of it to Hughes. Guerin and Wild owner Craig Leipold already made a big statement last year by making Kirill Kaprizov the highest-paid player in the game, at least for a moment.

items.body: It’s American Thanksgiving. Do you know where your NHL team is? The U.S. holiday has long served as an unofficial measuring stick to gauge teams’ likelihood of making the playoffs. Put simply, clubs sitting in playoff position at this time of year have a roughly 75 per cent chance of remaining there by season’s end. While far from a perfect rule, it’s generally pretty accurate. Take the past two seasons, for example — of the 16 teams inside the playoff window at Thanksgiving in back-to-back years, 12 ultimately clinched a spot. The rate was higher in 2022-23 and 2023-24, with 13 sitting and staying in a playoff spot. To round out our five-year sample size of recent examples, the 2021-22 campaign also showed a 75 per cent clinch rate of teams in playoff position at the U.S. Thanksgiving mark. When we think about noteworthy exceptions to this benchmark, the 2018-19 St. Louis Blues always jump to mind. By Thanksgiving of that season, the team was sitting last in the Central, lagging seven points behind the Dallas Stars for the second wild card spot, and had just made a coaching change by firing Mike Yeo and promoting Craig Berube in his place. (Of course, what made that squad particularly special was the fact they remained in last place early into the new calendar year, not launching their dramatic and historic comeback until January.) items.title: Zdeno Chara joins Hockey Hall of Fame selection committee
items.summary: Chara played 24 seasons in the NHL and won the Stanley Cup in 2011, as well as the Norris Trophy in 2009.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images The Hockey Hall of Fame announced Thursday that former NHL defenseman Zdeno Chara has been appointed to its selection committee . Chara, who was inducted into the Hall of Fame in 2025, will replace fellow inductee Igor Larionov. The Hall of Fame selection committee has 18 members and each serves a 15-year term. “It’s a true honor to be asked to serve on the Hockey Hall of Fame Selection Committee,” said Chara. “This game has given me so much throughout my life, and I take seriously the responsibility of helping recognize the individuals who have shaped its history and legacy. I am grateful for this opportunity.” The New York Islanders selected Chara in the third round of the 1996 NHL Draft. Throughout his 24-year NHL career, he skated with the Islanders, Ottawa Senators , Boston Bruins and Washington Capitals . A Slovak native, he recorded 209 goals and 471 assists for 680 points and 2,085 penalty minutes. At 1,680 career regular-season games, he ranks seventh on the NHL’s all-time games played list, and is 36th in points among NHL defenders. He reached the 50-point mark three times in his career and recorded a career-high 19 goals in 2008-09. He also finished with 40 assists and 52 points in 2011-12. He also dressed in 200 playoff games, where he scored 18 goals and added 52 assists for 70 points. He captained the Bruins to a Stanley Cup championship in 2011 and helped them reach the Final in both 2013 and 2019. Chara won the Norris Trophy in 2008-09 and was a five-time finalist in his career. Chara was inducted in 2025 along with Joe Thornton, Duncan Keith, Jennifer Botterill and Brianna Decker. items.summary: The former Montreal Canadiens star announced the end of his 16-year NHL career on his wife’s podcast.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Longtime NHL defenseman Jeff Petry is hanging up his skates, announcing his retirement from the league at 38 on a recent episode of the “Never Offside” podcast with his wife, Julie and Cat Toffoli, wife of San Jose Sharks forward Tyler Toffoli. Petry had not played at all in 2026-27, last lacing up in 2025-26 when he netted eight assists in 58 games across time with the Florida Panthers and Minnesota Wild . In the three years prior, he also played for the Pittsburgh Penguins and Detroit Red Wings . Yet, he is best known for his time with the Edmonton Oilers and Montreal Canadiens . Selected 45th overall by Edmonton in 2006, he played parts of five seasons in Alberta before the Canadiens acquired him in 2015, where he established himself as a consistent two-way blueline presence. During his time with the Canadiens, he posted four back-to-back seasons with 40 or more points from 2017-18 to 2020-21, with his career high a 13-goal, 33-assist campaign while playing all 82 games in 2018-19. His contributions, largely in front of recently inducted Hockey Hall of Fame netminder Carey Price, helped the Canadiens reach the 2020-21 Stanley Cup Final in the NHL’s second COVID-19-impacted season, where they fell to the Tampa Bay Lightning . The Ann Arbor, Mich., native wraps up his career with 96 goals and 394 points in 1,048 regular-season games, split between the Oilers, Canadiens, Penguins, Red Wings, Panthers and Wild. He also made his presence known internationally, suiting up for the USA four times at the IIHF World Championship, claiming a bronze medal at the 2013 tournament in Sweden and Finland. items.body: A recent Hockey Hall of Fame inductee will help decide who joins him. Zdeno Chara has been appointed to the Hockey Hall of Fame's selection committee, they announced on Thursday. Chara, who was added to the hall with the 2025 class in his first year of eligibility, played in the NHL for 24 seasons and became a Stanley Cup champion with the Boston Bruins in 2011. In 2009, he was awarded the James Norris Memorial Trophy for his outstanding year with the Bruins. He was a six-time NHL All-Star and captained the Bruins for 14 seasons. The 49-year-old will take the spot of fellow Hall of Famer Igor Larionov, whose 15-year term serving on the committee has ended. The committee is made up of 18 members who determine who will be added to the hall each November.

items.summary: A fight between two willing players, or a response to a dirty hit, is part of how hockey polices itself and part of what makes it special. But something has changed in how players react to legal hits. The old approach was to spring into action after an egregious or illegal hit and, after a […]
items.body: Register Login Have Fights And Scrums After Clean Hits Become An Issue? By Ryan Long | at November 26, 2026 9:39 am A fight between two willing players, or a response to a dirty hit, is part of how hockey polices itself and part of what makes it special. But something has changed in how players react to legal hits. The old approach was to spring into action after an egregious or illegal hit and, after a big clean hit on a teammate, remember the number and settle it later. Now the reflex is to go after the hitter the moment the whistle blows, often halfheartedly, whether the hit was clean or not. So have fights and scrums after clean hits become an issue? The numbers say they have, and the league has had a tool to deal with them for more than three decades. A Pro Hockey Rumors review of NHL play-by-play data from all 399 regular-season games through Nov. 25 found 110 fights. Forty-three of them, or 39.1%, came within 10 seconds of a hit that drew no penalty, with no faceoff in between. In 32 of those 43 fights, one of the combatants was the player who delivered the hit. The instigator penalty was called seven times in those 43 fights. Only eight instigator penalties have been called league-wide this season. In 28 of the 43, the responding team received no penalty beyond the matching fighting majors. The fights are only part of it. Another 60 unpenalized hits this season were followed by roughing calls but no fight. That’s 1.4 of those scrums for every fight after a legal hit, and none of them show up in fight totals. items.summary: More seasons than not, we see bench bosses fired before Christmas. Who’s in danger?
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources American Thanksgiving represents a fascinating point in the NHL season because the sample sizes are large enough to matter for struggling teams, yet the season is just young enough that it’s still possible to save it in rare cases. The most famous example: the 2018-19 St. Louis Blues, who named Craig Berube interim head coach in November and rose from dead last in the NHL standings as late as Jan. 2 to winning the Stanley Cup. Maybe a case study like that gives teams false hope, maybe not. But we do frequently see firings start to pop up around this time of year in the NHL. In 2023-24, we saw four head coach firings before the league reached its late-December holiday break. The 2024-25 season had four bench bosses axed between Nov. 19 and Dec. 26 alone. The first pink slip of 2025-26 came in mid-January. Recent history thus tells us it’s not too soon to run a temperature check of every seat in the league. Which coaches are in the most trouble right now? These bench bosses are going strong, with no job jeopardy whatsoever based on current results and/or being new hires. Nothing to discuss here. items.body: Register Login Brenden Dillon To Have Hearing For Hit On Denton Mateychuk By Ryan Long | at November 26, 2026 8:31 am Devils defenseman Brenden Dillon will have a hearing with the NHL Department of Player Safety today for an illegal check to the head/interference on Blue Jackets defenseman Denton Mateychuk , the league announced . The league hasn’t said whether the hearing will be by phone or in person. A phone hearing would cap any suspension at five games, while an in-person hearing would allow for a longer one. The hit came at 12:54 of the first period of New Jersey’s 3-2 shootout win in Columbus last night. Dillon caught Mateychuk in the Devils’ defensive zone and got a five-minute major and a match penalty. That ended his night after four shifts and 3:23 of ice time. Mateychuk went down hard and did not return. Columbus head coach Rick Bowness said afterward that the former 12th overall pick was fine and that concussion protocol would take over. New Jersey killed off the major and won on Arseny Gritsyuk ’s shootout goal, improving to 17-8-0 on the season. Dillon has been here before. In February 2024, while with the Jets, he was suspended three games and forfeited nearly $61K in salary for an illegal check to the head of Penguins forward Noel Acciari , which also drew a match penalty. Last November, he was fined $5K, the maximum allowable under the CBA, for boarding Blackhawks forward Tyler Bertuzzi . He also served a one-game suspension with the Sharks in December 2017 for slashing Capitals defenseman Madison Bowey . Because more than 18 months have passed since his last suspension, Dillon isn’t considered a repeat offender under the CBA, which affects only how much salary he’d forfeit. The Department of Player Safety can still weigh his full disciplinary history

items.summary: The Sirens improved (slightly) last season, but are facing another uphill battle heading into Year 4.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: PWHL LAST SEASON The New York Sirens have arguably been the biggest disappointment in the first three years of the PWHL. While the other five teams from the Original Six have managed to make the Walter Cup Playoffs twice, the team has bounced around from Connecticut to Long Island to New Jersey and has fallen short of playing beyond the regular season. There was some promise in 2025-26. After finishing dead last in each of the first two years of the league, the Sirens possessed a strong young offensive core that seemed poised to fight for one of the last two postseason positions. However, just like in seasons past, New York stumbled at the worst time of the season. The team lost eight of nine from January and beyond the Olympic Break, sending the team toward the bottom of the league. After falling out of playoff contention (again), the Sirens were unable to earn the No. 1 pick for the third year in a row, ultimately finishing seventh in the PWHL with a 9-3-3-15 record, eight points back of fourth place. items.title: Canadiens’ Florian Xhekaj receives match penalty for slew foot
items.body: It was a chippy affair between the Montreal Canadiens and Colorado Avalanche on Wednesday night, and Florian Xhekaj was right in the middle of all of it. It culminated late in the third period, when the forward was handed a match penalty for slew-footing Avalanche forward Fedor Svechkov, subsequently ending his night. The infraction happened with just over a minute remaining in the game as the Canadiens were down 6-0. The whistle had just sounded when Xhekaj tripped up Svechkov and was assessed an intent-to-injure penalty. That would be five of Xhekaj's 22 penalty minutes on the evening, as he was also assessed a 10-minute misconduct in the second period. A match penalty comes with an automatic ejection and review from the league. Florian wouldn't be the only Xhekaj to amass a fair few PIMs on Wednesday, as brother Arber — a Canadiens defenceman — wracked up 16 of his own. The brothers combined for 33 of the 42 total penalty minutes in this game. Avalanche captain Gabriel Landeskog wasn't thrilled with the antics of the Xhekaj brothers, telling reporters that they "have to use (their) head a little bit." "The Xhekaj brothers, they wanted to get involved so we'll see what's going to happen with that," Landeskog told reporters after the game . "I think for one of the most storied franchises and one of the most respected franchises in all of hockey, and you've got two guys doing that." Florian, who has played 17 career NHL games, has 54 penalty minutes. There will be no chance for revenge, though, on either side as Wednesday's match wrapped up the season series between the two inter-conference teams.

items.body: ST. PAUL, Minn. — Logan Cooley and Dylan Guenther each had a goal and an assist for the Utah Mammoth , in a 4-3 win on Wednesday night that gave the Minnesota Wild their first regulation loss in 16 games. Blake Coleman had two goals and Bobby Brink also scored for the Western Conference-leading Wild (18-4-5), who were a franchise-best 12-0-3 in their previous 15 games. After Coleman cut the deficit to one with 4:04 left, Mammoth center Barret Hayton was whistled 19 seconds later for a double-minor penalty for high-sticking Joel Eriksson Ek. The Wild had a power play for the remainder of regulation but managed only two shots. Karel Vejmelka made 22 saves for his first win in seven starts since Oct. 24 and Lawson Crouse and Dmitri Simashev scored for the Mammoth, whose second-period leads of 3-1 and 4-2 gave the Wild a two-goal deficit for the first time since their last regulation loss at Calgary on Oct. 22. Crouse’s tip-in of Vincent Trocheck’s shot in the first period stopped Minnesota’s scoring-first streak at 15 straight games. That was tied for the second-longest run in NHL history and best in the league since Montreal in 1972. The Canadiens have the record with 18 consecutive games, set during the 1959-60 season. Kirill Kaprizov’s franchise-record streak of 15 straight games with a point ended, as did his run of six consecutive games with multiple assists. That was the second-longest streak in NHL history, behind Wayne Gretzky's eight in 1984. Kaprizov went without a point for just the third time in 27 games, with linemates Eriksson Ek and Matt Boldy also producing at a prolific rate this season. The Wild played without star defenseman Quinn Hughes for the third straight game with an undisclosed injury.

items.title: Ducks’ Cutter Gauthier becomes first American to score 21 goals in 14 games
items.body: Only three full seasons into his NHL career, Cutter Gauthier is rewriting record books. The Anaheim Ducks star forward has been on a near-unparalleled scoring surge in recent weeks, and after yet another goal against the San Jose Sharks on Wednesday night, he hit a mark last reached by Mario Lemieux more than three decades ago. With his 21st goal in the last 14 games, Gauthier became the first player to accomplish the feat since Lemieux in the 1992-93 season, and became the only American in NHL history to do so. He hit the mark with just under five minutes left in the first period against the Sharks, finishing off a power-play marker set up by Jackson LaCombe and Mikael Granlund to give his side a 3-0 lead. The only other players to score 21 in 14 games are Lemieux (1992-93 and 1988-89), Teeme Selanne (1992-93), Alexander Mogilny (1992-93), Bernie Nichols (1988-89) and Wayne Gretzky (1980-81, 1981-82, and 1983-84). Gauthier's run started on Oct. 29, when he potted two goals against the Buffalo Sabres. He went on to score back-to-back hat tricks against the Ottawa Senators and Vancouver Canucks, then grabbed two more against the Pittsburgh Penguins and St. Louis Blues over the course of his streak. With the majority of his goals — 19 of them — coming since the calendar turned to November, he may set the record for most goals in a calendar month in the coming days, with Selanne atop the ladder with 20. Gauthier is only the eighth player and second American to score 19 in a calendar month, and has two more games against the Los Angeles Kings on Nov. 27 and 28 to break the record. On the season, the 22-year-old has 23 goals — tied for the league lead with Leon Draisaitl of the Edmonton Oilers — and nine assists in 25 games.

items.body: Register Login Injury Notes: Holmberg, Hedman, Cernak, Miller, Bertuzzi By Bradley Keith | at November 25, 2026 10:25 pm The Tampa Bay Lightning announced mid-game that Pontus Holmberg was injured against Carolina and would not return. Known to be a dependable shutdown winger, Holmberg has shown new elements to his game, being rewarded with time on the power play as well as a top six deployment, including tonight on Brayden Point ’s wing. Going 7-4-0 since star Nikita Kucherov ’s unexpected and league-shaking trade request , the Bolts lost to Carolina tonight and haven’t had the smoothest past few days. Last Sunday the superstar was benched in a convincing loss to Buffalo. Through it all, Holmberg has stayed in Cooper’s good graces, earning more shifts that night and continuing to cement himself as a vital middle-six role player. items.title: Canucks fall to Red Wings as Finnie, Arvidsson have three points each
items.body: DETROIT — Emmitt Finnie scored two early goals to lead the Detroit Red Wings to a 5-1 victory over the Vancouver Canucks on Wednesday night in a battle of last-place teams. Finnie added an assist and Viktor Arvidsson had a goal and two assists for Detroit, which had lost seven of eight. Lucas Raymond and J.T. Compher also scored and Daniil Tarasov made 25 saves. Vancouver had won three of five since breaking a 1-16-1 skid. Finnie got his first at 1:16, tipping in Arvidsson's shot from the right wing, then made it 2-0 at 4:05 by knocking in the rebound of Marco Kasper's shot. Finnie was the first Red Wings player to score twice in the first five minutes of a game since Brett Hull had two in the first 3:56 of a 5-2 win over the St. Louis Blues on Jan. 26, 2002. Hull finished that game with five points — three goals and two assists. Raymond made it 3-0 with a power-play goal with 57 seconds left in the first. Moritz Seider fed him the puck at the right faceoff spot, and he beat a screened Merilainen for his 10th goal of the season. Compher got Detroit's fourth goal at 6:24 of the second period, tapping in Michael Brandsegg-Nygard's pass at the back post. Paul Cotter ruined Tarasov's shutout bid with a goal at 7:26 of the third, but Arvidsson restored the four-goal lead at 8:08. Anton Lundell, Sam Bennett, Niko Mikkola and Eetu Luostarinen also had goals for Florida, which got both Marchand and Barkov back after each missed nearly two months with knee injuries suffered in the season's opening week. Dylan Cozens and Philip Tomasino had goals 41 seconds apart early in the second period for Ottawa, with Artem Zub and Jake Sanderson picking up assists on both as the Senators took a 2-1 lead. Mikkola tied it for Florida midway through the second period and Marchand — stickhandling around a pair of Senators — set up Lundell for the goal that gave the Panthers a 3-2 lead going into the third. Bennett's goal with 10:43 left sealed it, beating Ottawa goalie Linus Ullmark from close range for a 4-2 lead. The play started with Florida goalie Jacob Markstrom coming way out of the net, nearly to the blue line, to send a loose puck to the right-wing boards. Marchand played it to Lundell, who set up Bennett. Ullmark entered the game as the NHL's leader this season with a 1.44 goals-against average and a .938 save percentage. The Panthers solved him, becoming the first team to score four on Ullmark this season. In his first 13 appearances this season, Ullmark allowed three goals only once — in a 4-3 overtime win over Colorado on Nov. 12.

items.summary: Morgan Barron scored the tie-breaking goal late in the second period, Nico Daws made 21 saves, and the Winnipeg Jets added to their surge with a 4-2 victory over the Boston Bruins on Wednesday night.
items.body: BOSTON — Morgan Barron scored the tie-breaking goal late in the second period, Nico Daws made 21 saves, and the Winnipeg Jets added to their surge with a 4-2 victory over the Boston Bruins on Wednesday night. Kyle Connor and Josh Morrissey each had a goal for Winnipeg, which won its fourth straight road game and improved to 9-1-1 in its last 11 overall. Mark Scheifele, the Jets' career goals leader, added an empty-netter for the 381st of his career. Morgan Geekie and Fraser Minten scored for the Bruins, who dropped the second of their season-high six-game homestand. Jeremy Swayman stopped 14 shots. Barron’s goal came with 2:07 left in the second when he poked the puck between Swayman’s pads to make it 3-2 after the goalie mishandled the rebound of Mario Ferraro’s shot. Boston’s Tanner Jeannot and Winnipeg’s Tyrel Bauer squared off in a lengthy fight midway into the opening period that featured numerous haymakers. Trailing in the second, Boston tied it at 2 when Minten, positioned directly in front of the net, tipped Mason Lohrei’s shot by Daws at 10:57. Morrissey’s slap shot from the slot beat Swayman and gave the Jets a 2-1 edge late in the opening period. Off since a 7-5 victory over Washington at home Saturday, the Bruins had tied it at 1 on Geekie’s power-play goal off a pretty pass across the front of the net by David Pastrnak at 6:11. Connor’s wrister from the left circle made it 1-0 just 65 seconds into the game. The Bruins won the first meeting between the teams in overtime on Oct. 2.

items.title: Farabee has goal and assist to help Flames beat Penguins
items.body: PITTSBURGH — Joel Farabee had a goal and an assist and the Calgary Flames beat the Pittsburgh Penguins 6-3 on Wednesday night. Maxim Tsyplakov and Brennan Othmann also each had a goal and an assist for the Flames, who snapped a three-game losing streak. Ryan Strome, Jonathan Castagna and Yegor Sharangovich also scored. Zayne Parekh had an assist to pass Miles Zaharko for the fifth-most points by a Flames’ defenceman younger than 21. Evgeni Malkin passed Bryan Trottier for 19th-most points in NHL history with a power-play goal and an assist for Pittsburgh. Malkin, who missed the last two games because of an injury, had his 382nd multipoint game and tied Teemu Selanne for fourth among players born and trained outside of North America. Rickard Rakell also had a power-play goal and Tommy Novak also scored. The Penguins scored two home power-play goals for the first time since an Oct. 3 win against Montreal. Arturs Silovs stopped 20 shots for the Penguins, who lost their fifth straight. Pittsburgh, last in the Eastern Conference, has lost 10 of 12 overall. The Flames won their 64th straight game when scoring four or more goals. They’re one four-goal win from tying the New York Rangers’ 65-game run from 2011-14, the longest mark in NHL history. The streak began with a 4-2 victory over Tampa Bay on Dec. 16, 2023. This season, the Flames are 7-0-0 when scoring at least four goals.

items.body: Register Login Ducks Recall Laurent Brossoit By Brennan McClain | at November 25, 2026 6:00 pm The Anaheim Ducks will have their oldest netminder back in the starters’ crease this evening. According to a team announcement , the Ducks recalled goaltender Laurent Brossoit from the San Diego Gulls in the AHL, and he will start tonight against the San Jose Sharks. Technically, tonight’s contest will be Brossoit’s first against his former team. Still, he didn’t have a lengthy history with the Sharks organization. In 2024, the Chicago Blackhawks signed Brossoit to a two-year, $6.6MM contract in free agency. Unfortunately, hip and knee injuries prevented him from playing a game with the Blackhawks. Chicago traded Brossoit to San Jose last January. By the time his contract ended, Brossoit had appeared in only one game with the Sharks. Regardless, he landed on his feet this past summer, inking a one-year, $1MM deal with the Ducks as their third-string netminder. On Halloween, after Anaheim had lost seven of their last eight contests, they recalled Brossoit to debut with the club. Although his save percentage (.867 SV%) and goals-against average (3.42) weren’t good, Anaheim won four of Brossoit’s five appearances, effectively turning their season around. Unfortunately, since Brossoit’s last start on November 11th, the Ducks are in a similar situation. They’ve lost five of their six matchups since Brossoit was reassigned. Mandatory Credit: David Kirouac-Imagn Images Anyone anticipating Patrik Laine’s return to the NHL is going to have to wait a good while longer. On Wednesday, the winger announced via Instagram that he recently underwent knee surgery, and is expecting a lengthy rehab and recovery. Laine, 28, played in the first five games of last season for the Montreal Canadiens before suffering what was initially classified as a lower-body injury. He then underwent core muscle surgery, which kept him out for the remainder of the regular season and playoffs, though he later suggested that he could’ve returned in January. The exact injury this most recent surgery was intended to repair is unclear, though he did miss 24 games with a left knee sprain during the 2024-25 season. The Finnish national entered this past offseason as an unrestricted free agent, but has yet to be signed and is currently without an NHL contract. Selected second overall by the Winnipeg Jets in the 2016 NHL Entry Draft, Laine has had a tumultuous career thus far. Draft-eligible players can cement themselves as top prospects, and drafted prospects can compete against the world's best while representing their country at a major event. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Colorado Avalanche star Cale Makar is set to return to the lineup for Wednesday’s game against the Montreal Canadiens after missing the past three games with a lower-body injury. Makar, 28, sustained the injury during Colorado’s 4-3 overtime loss to the Ottawa Senators at the Canadian Tire Centre on Nov. 12. The 6’0″ right-shot defender confirmed that he’s “ready to go” after the team’s morning skate on Wednesday. The Avalanche remain without leading scorer Nathan MacKinnon, who is expected to miss three months while recovering from a lower-body injury of his own, but Makar is expected to be active when the Canadiens and Avalanche hit the ice at Ball Arena in Denver. Through 19 games with the Avalanche to start the 2026-27 regular season, Makar has five goals and 23 points while averaging 22:25 of ice time. Shortly before the start of the team’s 2026 training camp, Makar and the Avalanche agreed to terms on an eight-year contract extension that will pay him $20.4 million per year through 2035. The Avalanche originally selected Makar with the No. 4 overall pick in the 2017 NHL Draft. After spending two seasons at UMass-Amherst, Makar debuted with the Avalanche during the 2019 Stanley Cup Playoffs and immediately established himself as their top defender. He won the Calder Memorial Trophy as the NHL’s top rookie in the 2019-20 season. Two years later, Makar played an instrumental role in the Avalanche winning the Stanley Cup, scoring 29 points in 20 postseason games en route to receiving the Conn Smythe Trophy as playoff MVP. items.body: Register Login Ducks Reassign Noah Warren By Brennan McClain | at November 25, 2026 12:00 pm Yesterday afternoon, the Anaheim Ducks announced they reassigned defenseman Noah Warren to the San Diego Gulls in the AHL. The transaction drops Anaheim to 22 players on the active roster. Until yesterday, Warren had been a constant on the Ducks’ defensive corps all season. After playing two years for the Gulls, the former 42nd overall pick cracked Anaheim’s opening-night roster to begin the 2026-27 campaign. In San Diego, Warren registered two goals and 16 points in 122 games from 2024 to 2026. There’s no question the 6’5″, 216lbs defender isn’t known for his offensive skills. Still, Warren didn’t look entirely out of place with the Ducks this season, tallying six assists in 23 contests on a -3 rating while averaging 15:33 of ice time per game. Regardless of yesterday’s demotion, Warren should expect to hold down a long-term spot with the Ducks relatively soon. Anaheim lost multiple defenders this past offseason, and although he likely won’t contribute a ton offensively, Warren’s mobility, especially at his size, makes him a useful talent to have on the back end. Meanwhile, the Ducks could go multiple different directions with their newfound roster spot. Currently, Anaheim is waiting for forwards A.J. Greer and Beckett Sennecke to return from injury. Both Greer and Sennecke are projected to return toward the end of November, so the Ducks may activate one of them soon.

items.title: Was a missed too-many-men call good gamesmanship from the Golden Knights?
items.summary: Jack Eichel scored twice as Vegas defeated their Pacific Division rivals in Edmonton 5-3 on Tuesday night.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Vegas Golden Knights defeated the Edmonton Oilers 5-3 Tuesday night. Jack Eichel scored twice, the second being the game-winning goal early in the third period. Some Edmonton fans said the officials missed a too-many-men penalty right before Eichel buried his 11th of the season, while others claimed it was simply an example of gamesmanship on the Golden Knights’ behalf. On Wednesday’s episode of Daily Faceoff LIVE , Tyler Yaremchuk and former NHL goaltender Carter Hutton discuss the play and whether the refs missed a penalty late in the game. Tyler Yaremchuk : There were five Golden Knights on the ice … watch Jack Eichel, right at the top. He’s going to jump on the boards for William Karlsson, but Karlsson is still engaged in a battle with both Kasperi Kapanen and Mattias Ekholm … he’s still engaged and preventing an Edmonton Oiler from coming back into the rush to backcheck and provide some amount of back pressure. Eichel jumps over the boards, and you can tell no one on Edmonton is looking for Eichel there because there’s already five players on the ice. Everyone has already picked up a man. Vegas gains a massive advantage … Eichel jumps on the ice as a sixth attacker, totally undetected, and he walks in and ends up scoring. Is this a missed call or is this good gamesmanship from Vegas? items.title: Frost sign Sara Swiderski to three-year contract
items.summary: Ohio State’s Swiderski was selected by Minnesota in the first round of the 2026 PWHL Draft.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: PWHL The Minnesota Frost announced Wednesday that defender Sara Swiderski has been signed to a three-year contract through the 2028-29 season. Swiderski, taken No. 9 overall in the first round of the 2026 PWHL Draft, is coming off a highly productive senior season of college hockey with The Ohio State University where she scored eight goals and recorded 19 assists for 27 points in 33 games. “I am looking forward to the opportunity to learn from the amazing coaches here and play alongside some incredibly skilled players, especially those on the blue line,” Swiderski, a native of Langley, B.C., said in a news release. In four seasons spent between Ohio State and Clarkson University, Swiderski had 13 goals and 45 assists for 58 points in 148 career NCAA games. “We are thrilled that Sara has committed to the Frost for the next three seasons,” Frost general manager Melissa Caruso said in the news release. “She is a highly mobile two-way defender who will contribute immediately to the Frost’s D core.” Minnesota went 13-3-5-9 with 50 points in 2025-26, good for third in the league standings. They were eliminated by the eventual Walter Cup-champion Montreal Victoire in five games in the first round of the PWHL playoffs. Kelly Pannek was named Forward of the Year and finished with a PWHL record-breaking 33 points . She also won both the Points Leader and Top Goal Scorer awards .

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Michal Postava (Nicolas Carrillo/Grand Rapids Griffins) Goalies are the most fun prospects to talk about. It’s such a difficult position to judge. So when someone, especially a guy who hasn’t received a ton of love in the media, ends up going on a hot streak, you can’t help but notice. The AHL is a grind. And while most teams like to rotate their goalies throughout a weekend, there are still plenty of opportunities for a young netminder to prove they have a real NHL future. A handful of the AHL’s top goalies last year are playing full-time in the NHL – most notably Boston’s Michael DiPietro, Montreal’s Jacob Fowler and New York’s Dylan Garand. With a quarter of the AHL season complete, let’s look at five goalie prospects making waves in the top development league in the world. One of them has already been called up to the NHL this season, and it’s only a matter of time until a few more get their opportunity: Nabokov was one of the best KHL goaltenders for three years before finally coming over to North America this season. He’s been just as advertised with a solid .920 save percentage, including some real tight affairs along the way. Longtime AHLer Trent Miner is currently out with an injury, but Nabokov has been better than him, all things considered. It’s not too surprising; Nabokov was considered one of the top goaltending prospects from the 2024 NHL Draft thanks to his pure athleticism and quick hands. Nov. 22nd: The Florida Panthers are nearing a fully healthy roster. According to George Richards of Florida Hockey Now , the Panthers are expected to activate captain Aleksander Barkov from the long-term injured reserve on Wednesday. Additionally, veteran winger Brad Marchand will likely return on Wednesday also. Even if only Barkov returns on Wednesday, he alone would make a significant difference in Florida’s outlook. The fact that they could return both Barkov and Marchand is a different story entirely. The Panthers haven’t had Barkov since the first day of October, and haven’t had Marchand since October 6th. Hopefully, for Barkov’s sake, he can maintain some semblance of health for the foreseeable future. After the Panthers repeated as Stanley Cup champions in 2025, Barkov damaged his ACL and MCL leading up to the 2025-26 campaign. Some hoped Barkov could return before the end of the season or the playoffs, but neither happened. items.body: NEW YORK CITY — There are two doors standing before the 2026-27 Toronto Maple Leafs and their die-hard fans. Or perhaps the hopeful message six-year-old fan Wyatt Warner scratched on white Bristol board with a royal-blue Sharpie and, with the blessing of Mats Sundin, brought into the team’s dressing room Monday night, following its resilient 4-2 comeback win on Long Island: BELIEVE IN YOURSELVES. IT TAKES ONE. YOU GOT THIS . The agent for the injured Kirill Marchenko, who was last playing for the Leafs when they were still in the hunt, is choosing to walk through that door. Dan Milstein pointed to the 2019 Blues and 2012 Kings and 2009 Penguins, reminding those teams’ troublesome starts — even if those starts ran two or three months — were eventually spun into storybook endings. “Whatever team you cheer for, don’t give up on them,” Milstein urged via X . “Players care, and they need your support.” Athletes have no choice but faith, to look at the 58 games remaining on the schedule — not the 2.5 per cent playoff odds on MoneyPuck.com — and see possibility. “Just keep on keepin’ on,” veteran Jake McCabe said of the path forward during November’s nine-game losing skid. “There’s no magic recipe.” Let’s call it Lloyd Christmas magic, then. There is something wonderful about being part of the “ So, you’re telling me there’s a chance ” crowd. Hey, sports are unpredictable. Bouncing rubber on frozen water and all that. Anything can happen, right? That’s why we tune in and they tune the critics out. Over the other door hangs a motto straight out of The Shawshank Redemption , with a caveat.
